aboutGame.title: What is 1 Upgrade Per Kill?
paragraphs: 1 Upgrade Per Kill is a free-to-play Roblox free-for-all PvP arena from Block PvP. Every elimination advances your armor one step along a 34-step ladder, from Leather through Copper, Iron, Full Diamond, Ruby, Shadow, and Prism to MAXED.

Eight classes reshape how you fight, while Gold buys perks, enchants add build variety, and Golden Apples keep a winning trade alive. Death normally resets the ladder, but a Gear Saver can preserve your armor. Our guides cover codes, classes, upgrade tiers, combat, and Gold routes.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Codes
modules.description: Redeem the confirmed WELCOME code for a free gift, claim the separate Block PvP group reward, and learn the lobby redemption flow.

highlights.label: WELCOME
highlights.detail: Free gift plus a prompt to join the Block PvP group for a second gift.

highlights.label: GROUP
highlights.detail: Join the Block PvP group to claim the separate community reward.

highlights.label: REDEEM
highlights.detail: Open the code menu in the lobby, paste the all-caps code, submit, and check your inventory.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Beginner Guide
modules.description: Follow the first-match loop from class selection and safe target picking to Gold spending, Golden Apple timing, and streak protection.

highlights.detail: Pick Warrior for your first sessions; its extra Golden Apples leave room to learn the arena.
Win one safe fight at a time and avoid fair duels while your armor is still Leather.
Bank Gold from daily quests, bounties, kills, and the playtime track before buying perks.
Use Golden Apples before your health empties; one lost stack costs more than one apple.
Save a Gear Saver for Shadow or above, when a death would erase several tiers.
Redeem WELCOME in the lobby and claim the Block PvP group gift before queueing.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Classes Guide
modules.description: Compare all eight classes by combat role, range, mobility, and escape tools, then choose a kit that matches your arena instincts.

highlights.label: Warrior
highlights.detail: Melee bruiser with extra Golden Apples for straight duels and holding ground.

highlights.label: Archer
highlights.detail: Ranged pressure for chipping targets before committing to a fight.

highlights.label: Trickster
highlights.detail: Mobility and misdirection for escaping bad fights and stealing third-party kills.

highlights.label: Trapper
highlights.detail: Area control that locks down chokepoints and stops enemy combos.

highlights.label: Skirmisher
highlights.detail: Hit-and-run pressure for quick kills and fast disengages.

highlights.label: Fire
highlights.detail: Firestarter deals damage over time that softens groups and denies space.

highlights.label: Bomber
highlights.detail: Burst and explosives for punishing clustered players.

highlights.label: Scorcher
highlights.detail: Aggressive pressure built to snowball early kills and break armor.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Upgrade Tiers
modules.description: Track the 34-step armor ladder from Leather to MAXED and learn which stages reward patience, consolidation, and aggressive pushes.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: MAXED and Prism: the final ladder stages, where every fight can decide the run.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Shadow and Ruby: high-tier territory where survival matters more than another kill.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Full Diamond and Iron: the mid-game checkpoint with a dedicated Fastest Diamond leaderboard.

highlights.label: C
highlights.detail: Copper and Leather: the starting tiers, where safe third-party fights rebuild momentum.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Best Perks and Enchants
modules.description: Compare perks and enchant priorities that improve survivability, escape options, and damage without wasting Gold on cosmetics first.

highlights.label: Head Start
highlights.detail: Start each life with Leather pieces and no perk-slot cost.

highlights.label: Snack Pack
highlights.detail: Adds another Golden Apple per life for longer trades.

highlights.label: Mobility
highlights.detail: Movement and escape perks protect a high-upgrade streak.

highlights.label: Damage
highlights.detail: Damage enchants speed up kills and make the next tier easier to reach.

highlights.label: Gear Saver
highlights.detail: Keep your armor after one death when the stack is worth protecting.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Gold and Emeralds Guide
modules.description: Track Gold from kills, bounties, daily quests, the playtime track, and Server Boosts, then route it into perks, enchants, Golden Apples, and Gear Savers.

highlights.label: Kills
highlights.detail: Eliminations are the core Gold source and scale with your combat consistency.

highlights.label: Bounties
highlights.detail: Bounty targets add Gold once you can win fights consistently.

highlights.label: Quests
highlights.detail: Daily quests are the safest early income because they do not require a win.

highlights.label: Playtime
highlights.detail: The playtime track pays out even in rounds where you do not win.

highlights.label: Boosts
highlights.detail: Server Boosts raise Gold and XP gains but do not raise the upgrade counter.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Combat Tips and Strategies
modules.description: Use positioning, healing timing, target selection, edge awareness, and disengage rules to protect a growing upgrade stack.

highlights.label: Position
highlights.detail: Fight near cover and chokepoints so only one enemy can reach you at a time.

highlights.label: Healing
highlights.detail: Use Golden Apples before your health hits zero; a lost stack costs more than one apple.

highlights.label: Targets
highlights.detail: Hunt high-upgrade players for bonus XP only when you have a clear escape route.

highlights.label: Edges
highlights.detail: Stand two steps back from ledges; Trickster and Bomber can turn knockback into a kill.

highlights.label: Disengage
highlights.detail: At Ruby and above, walk away from a coin-flip fight instead of donating the ladder.

highlights.label: Cleanup
highlights.detail: Let two stacked players trade, then finish the survivor for a low-risk upgrade.

modules.name: 1 Upgrade Per Kill Shop and Game Passes
modules.description: Review Gear Savers, Gold-bought perks, class unlocks, crates, and capes, and separate combat value from cosmetic spending.

highlights.label: Gear Saver
highlights.detail: The safety net is worth banking for Shadow and above; avoid spending it at Iron.

highlights.label: Perks
highlights.detail: Gold-bought perks add long-term power outside a single streak.

highlights.label: Classes
highlights.detail: Warrior is free; Archer and Trickster are Robux unlocks; Bomber costs 4,000 Gold or a Halloween quest.

highlights.label: Crates
highlights.detail: Open crates for cosmetics and rewards that do not change the upgrade ladder.

highlights.label: Capes
highlights.detail: Capes are cosmetic status items and do not affect combat.

items.question: What is 1 Upgrade Per Kill?
items.answer: 1 Upgrade Per Kill is a free-to-play Roblox free-for-all PvP arena from Block PvP. Each elimination moves your armor one step up a 34-step ladder, while death normally resets the climb.

items.question: How does the upgrade ladder work in 1 Upgrade Per Kill?
items.answer: 1 Upgrade Per Kill uses eight named armor tiers: Leather, Copper, Iron, Full Diamond, Ruby, Shadow, Prism, and MAXED. The in-game counter tracks 34 total upgrade steps, with Full Diamond serving as a major mid-game checkpoint.

items.question: Does death reset progress in 1 Upgrade Per Kill?
items.answer: Yes. Dying in 1 Upgrade Per Kill normally returns your armor to Leather and clears the upgrade stack. A Gear Saver is the exception and can preserve your armor through one death.

items.question: Which class should beginners choose in 1 Upgrade Per Kill?
items.answer: Warrior is the most forgiving first class in 1 Upgrade Per Kill because its extra Golden Apples allow more mistakes. Once you learn the map, try mobile or ranged classes such as Trickster, Skirmisher, or Archer.

items.question: How do I redeem codes in 1 Upgrade Per Kill?
items.answer: Launch 1 Upgrade Per Kill, open the code menu in the lobby, paste WELCOME, submit it, and check your inventory. Joining the Block PvP group is a separate claim for a second gift.

items.question: What should I buy first in 1 Upgrade Per Kill?
items.answer: In 1 Upgrade Per Kill, prioritize a Gear Saver for high-tier runs, then choose perks and enchants that reinforce your class. Golden Apples support survival, while crates and capes are optional cosmetic spending.
